6. Cite real evidence_ids from supplied sources.
7. Message hex must be lowercase hexadecimal without separators.

The values marked RESERVED must not be interpreted as currently defined
standard operations.

================================================================
1. BACnet APDU PDU TYPE
================================================================

The APDU type is stored in the high nibble of the first APDU octet.

0x00 = Confirmed-Request-PDU
0x10 = Unconfirmed-Request-PDU
0x20 = SimpleACK-PDU
0x30 = ComplexACK-PDU
0x40 = SegmentACK-PDU
0x50 = Error-PDU
0x60 = Reject-PDU
0x70 = Abort-PDU

2 = SimpleACK-PDU
3 = ComplexACK-PDU
4 = SegmentACK-PDU
5 = Error-PDU
6 = Reject-PDU

[SOURCE id=issue:1270:1270-summary:f10b3cba62a1 kind=issue issue=1270 path=distilled_issue/1.BACnet-stack/#1270.txt]
Issue: 1270
Summary: In v1.3.1, the report says a malformed UCOV/property-value payload can make bacapp_decode_application_data() accept an oversized extended application length without checking it against the remaining APDU bytes. That unchecked length is then propagated through bacapp_decode_data() into host_n_port_decode(), which trusts it, and bacnet_tag_number_decode() eventually performs an invalid read and crashes. The observed result was an AddressSanitizer SEGV; GDB showed apdu_len_max=12, tag_len=7, len_value_type=0xFF210121, and tag_data_type=34 (BACNET_APPLICATION_TAG_HOST_N_PORT).
Reproduce: 1) Use v1.3.1. 2) Decode a malformed UCOV/property-value payload whose extended application length exceeds the remaining APDU bytes; the reported bytes near the triggering boundary were: f5 22 ff ff 21 01 21 0e 2d ff 00 e6. 3) In the failing case, GDB showed apdu_len_max=12, tag_len=7, len_value_type=0xFF210121, and tag_data_type=34 (BACNET_APPLICATION_TAG_HOST_N_PORT). 4) Expected result: the oversized length is accepted by bacapp_decode_application_data(), passed via bacapp_decode_data() into host_n_port_decode(), and bacnet_tag_number_decode() hits an invalid read, with AddressSanitizer reporting SEGV on an unknown address 0x641f9505e92e (pc 0x641f93a5ffdd bp 0x7ffeab919b70 sp 0x7ffeab919b50 T0).
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:cve-2026-41502:cve-2026-41502-summa:c282c210e609 kind=issue issue=2026 path=distilled_issue/1.BACnet-stack/#CVE-2026-41502.txt]
Issue: CVE-2026-41502
Summary: No affected version is specified. In `bacnet-stack`, `src/bacnet/rpm.c` function `rpm_decode_object_id()` checks `apdu_len < 5` even though it then consumes 6 bytes: a context tag at `apdu[0]`, a 4-byte object identifier at `apdu[1..4]`, and an opening-tag check at `apdu[5]`. A truncated 5-byte ReadPropertyMultiple object-identifier buffer therefore passes validation and causes a 1-byte out-of-bounds read when `decode_is_opening_tag_number()` and `decode_tag_number()` read past the buffer end. The supplied PoC demonstrates this by directly calling `rpm_decode_object_id()` with a 5-byte APDU. The report says deployments with the ReadPropertyMultiple confirmed service handler enabled, which is enabled by default in the reference server, are affected and that the read can lead to crashes on embedded BACnet devices.
Reproduce: No build configuration or commands are provided. The document’s PoC (`poc_rpm_off_by_one.c`) reproduces the issue by: 1. Including `bacnet/rpm.h`, zeroing a `BACNET_RPM_DATA` structure, and creating a 5-byte `apdu` buffer containing `0x0C` followed by `0x00 0x00 0x00 0x01` (context tag 0 plus a 4-byte object identifier for analog-input instance 1). 2. Calling `rpm_decode_object_id(apdu, 5, &rpmdata)`. 3. Expected result from the report: the `apdu_len < 5` check accepts the 5-byte input, `decode_is_context_tag()` reads `apdu[0]`, `decode_object_id()` reads `apdu[1..4]`, and `decode_is_opening_tag_number(&apdu[5], 1)` then reads one byte past the end of the buffer via `decode_tag_number()`. The report states that, when reached through the ReadPropertyMultiple service handler, this out-of-bounds read can crash embedded BACnet devices.
[/SOURCE]
